metadata.name: Acute pyelonephritis
metadata.specialty: Family medicine / Internal medicine / Urology / Paediatrics
metadata.emergency_level: Urgent; emergency with sepsis, obstruction or instability
metadata.severity: Potentially serious due to sepsis, abscess and renal injury

overview.short_description: Acute infection of the renal pelvis and kidney, typically causing fever, flank pain and systemic illness with or without lower urinary symptoms.
overview.detailed_description: Pyelonephritis requires prompt antibiotic treatment and urine culture. The central safety decision is whether oral outpatient treatment is safe or hospital care is required, and whether an obstructing stone or urinary abnormality is present.
overview.pathophysiology: Usually ascending bacterial infection from the lower tract reaches renal tissue; less often haematogenous spread. Obstruction impairs drainage and can convert infection into a urological emergency.
overview.etiology: Usually enteric bacteria; resistance depends on prior antibiotics, cultures, healthcare exposure and local data.
overview.natural_history: May progress rapidly to bacteraemia, sepsis, abscess or renal impairment without effective treatment/source control.
overview.prognosis: Good with prompt therapy; worse with obstruction, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression, renal disease or delayed treatment.

prevalence.value: Common serious bacterial infection encountered in urgent primary care

incidence.value: Varies by sex, age, pregnancy and urinary abnormality

mortality.value: Low in stable uncomplicated cases; meaningful with sepsis or obstruction

epidemiology.sex_predominance: More common with female urinary anatomy; men often require complicated-infection assessment

risk_factors.pregnancy: Requires lower threshold for specialist/hospital care
risk_factors.medications: Recent antibiotics alter resistance; immunosuppression raises severity
risk_factors.previous_diseases: UTI, stones, obstruction, reflux, catheter, prostate disease or urinary procedure

chief_complaints.complaint: Fever or shaking chills with flank/back pain
Nausea, vomiting or feeling systemically unwell

symptoms.symptom: Hypotension, confusion, oliguria or marked tachypnoea

negative_findings.finding: No fever, flank pain or systemic symptoms
negative_findings.why_important: Makes upper UTI less likely but does not exclude early disease

negative_findings.finding: Completely normal vital signs and good oral intake
negative_findings.why_important: Supports potential outpatient pathway only after full risk review

history_questions.question: Any fever, shaking, one-sided flank pain, nausea or vomiting?
Can you drink and keep medicines down?
Could you be pregnant, or is the patient a child/older frail person?
Any stones, poor urine flow, single kidney, catheter, urinary surgery or prostate disease?
Any diabetes, immunosuppression, renal disease, prior cultures or recent antibiotics?

physical_examination.examination: Full vital signs and sepsis assessment

physical_examination.expected_finding: Flank tenderness; assess for peritonism or distended bladder
Dehydration or oliguria may require hospital care

vital_signs.temperature: Often raised; normal temperature does not exclude
vital_signs.bmi: Record when relevant to risk or treatment

laboratory_tests.indication: Obtain before antibiotics when this does not delay urgent treatment
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range
Use current local laboratory reference range
Use current local laboratory reference range

laboratory_tests.indication: Sepsis/systemic illness before antibiotics when feasible
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Use current local laboratory reference range

imaging.imaging_type: Urgent renal ultrasound or CT according to context
imaging.when_needed: Suspected obstruction/stone, severe illness, renal impairment, atypical course or failure to improve
imaging.expected_findings: Hydronephrosis, stone, abscess or alternative diagnosis

ecg.when_needed: Not routine; use when cardiac disease, electrolyte disturbance or medicine risk indicates

other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Urine culture for all suspected acute pyelonephritis; blood cultures when septic
other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: Not routine unless another pathogen-specific indication exists

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Compatible upper-UTI syndrome (fever/systemic illness plus flank pain/tenderness, often with urinary symptoms) supported by urinalysis and urine culture; actively assess sepsis and obstruction.

diagnostic_scores.value: Use a validated sepsis assessment where indicated; no pyelonephritis-specific probability score is asserted.

diagnostic_criteria.cutoff_values: Use current sepsis, laboratory and local microbiology criteria; no universal cutoff authored.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Colic, hydronephrosis, anuria or stone history
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Colic, hydronephrosis, anuria or stone history
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any colicky pain, stone history or reduced urine?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Abrupt severe pain, vascular risk, less infectious pattern
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Abrupt severe pain, vascular risk, less infectious pattern
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Was pain sudden and are there embolic risks?
Any pelvic, pregnancy or focal abdominal features?

diagnostic_questions.question: Can the patient keep fluids and oral medicine down, and are vital signs stable?
Could there be a stone or urinary obstruction?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Obstruction plus infection requires urgent urology

next_best_question.question: Any sepsis, pregnancy, vomiting/dehydration, obstruction/stone, urinary abnormality, diabetes/immunosuppression or renal impairment?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Stable oral pathway versus hospital/urgent urology
next_best_question.branching_logic: Any major risk -> refer/seek specialist advice; stable low-risk -> culture and guideline-directed oral therapy with 48-hour reassessment

next_best_test.test: Urine culture before antibiotics when feasible
next_best_test.why: Therapy must be reviewed against susceptibility
Antibiotics alone do not resolve infected obstruction

red_flags.finding: Hypotension, confusion, oliguria, marked tachypnoea or other sepsis features
Fever with obstruction/stone, anuria or single kidney
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency urological assessment and source control

red_flags.finding: Pregnancy, significant dehydration or inability to take oral treatment
No improvement within 48 hours or worsening
red_flags.immediate_action: Reassess culture, resistance, obstruction, abscess and alternative diagnosis

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Pregnancy, dehydration/vomiting, significant comorbidity, structural urinary disease, child pathway or poor response.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Recurrent upper UTI or suspected structural abnormality after acute care.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Sepsis, infected obstruction, anuria, instability or organ dysfunction.

late: Renal scarring in selected paediatric/complicated cases

initial_management.supportive_care: Culture, assess sepsis/oral tolerance/obstruction, hydrate appropriately and start prompt guideline-directed antibiotics.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Paracetamol; Oral cephalosporin or susceptible beta-lactam; Fluoroquinolone; IV cephalosporin and/or aminoglycoside pathway. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG111_2024, NICE_NG224.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Fluids when safe; do not delay care for systemic deterioration.
initial_management.follow_up: Review culture and clinical response; reassess by 48 hours or sooner if worse.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Culture- and local-resistance-directed oral or IV antibiotic; restricted fluoroquinolone only when safer recommended options are inappropriate.

patient_education.home_advice: A kidney infection is more serious than a bladder infection. Fever, shaking, side/back pain and vomiting need prompt medical assessment and antibiotics.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: التهاب الكلية أخطر من التهاب المثانة. الحمى أو الرجفة أو ألم الخاصرة/الظهر أو القيء تحتاج تقييماً طبياً سريعاً ومضاداً حيوياً مناسباً.
patient_education.prevention: Investigate stones, obstruction or recurrent infections where indicated.
patient_education.warning_signs: Confusion, faintness, very low urine, worsening pain, persistent vomiting or failure to improve.

prevention.lifestyle: Address hydration and modifiable urinary-stasis risks
prevention.screening: Investigate recurrent or atypical infection according to age and risk

evidence.evidence_level: Guideline-grounded direction; no claim that every narrative sentence has clinician verification.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG111_2024, NICE_NG224; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

limitations: Guidelines require individual clinical judgement and may differ by country, formulary and antimicrobial resistance.
The evidence audit verifies traceability and major safety structure; it does not certify every narrative sentence.
No medication should be selected or dosed without patient-specific contraindication and interaction checking.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Treat acute upper UTI promptly, obtain culture, detect sepsis/obstruction and escalate patients who cannot safely receive oral outpatient care.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Paracetamol; Oral cephalosporin or susceptible beta-lactam; Fluoroquinolone; IV cephalosporin and/or aminoglycoside pathway. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG111_2024, NICE_NG224.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Adequate fluids when safe, urine culture before antibiotics when this does not delay treatment, and reassessment of culture/response.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Adjunct while definitive antibiotic treatment and hydration are arranged
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: severe active liver disease or prior serious reaction
use_caution_if: heavy alcohol use, malnutrition, low body weight, or concomitant paracetamol-containing products
monitoring: total daily exposure and clinical response

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Hospital referral for sepsis, obstruction/stone, pregnancy, severe dehydration, inability to take oral treatment, significant comorbidity/immunosuppression, infant/child pathway, or lack of improvement within 48 hours.
